??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Patch. I keep the herb house by the gate, which means I see the road's damage first. Mind your head on the bundles. Everybody hits that one.
    - You again. The one who can tell yarrow from hemlock. Come in. Do not touch the jars.
    - The lamp-hangers come in bitten and go out clean now, thanks to your peppery weed. They still look at me like I am the dangerous one. I am.
    - I have silent root drying in the rafters for the first time in four years. Every time I walk under it I think of the birds. Sit. Have a sweet. You earned three.
    - Well? I have patients.
        - *Choice:* What herbs do you need?
        - *Choice:* What is in Dagny's drink?
        - *Choice:* Who comes through your door?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - My mother sold herbs. Every summer morning she took me out past the gate and made me learn them: yarrow from hemlock, feverfew from chamomile, which roots in spring and which in autumn. Forty years I gathered my own.
    - Now my knees are slow, the fields are risky, and Brindle has told me to stop going out alone, first politely and then not. The carts bring less. And the herbs I need most grow where nobody sensible walks any more.
    - Willow bark, mostly. And something else. No, I will not tell you. If I told Dagny she would stop believing in it, and then it would stop working. She walks me home after, with both lamps. Unnecessary. Do not tell her I like it.
    - It used to be carters with barrels dropped on their feet and peddlers with blisters. Now it is bites, gashes, claw marks. In the middle of the night. Carried. More every season.
    - Ivo on the square sees them after me; we send them back and forth. I scold, he soothes, and between us we cover most kinds of person. What I am afraid of is the one I cannot help, and the morning after, when the jar I needed was empty.
    - Go on. And if you get bitten, walk here. Do not run.
